correctness.rationale: The 20 normalized dodecahedral vertices form exactly ten antipodal pairs with off-diagonal dot products ±1/3, ±√5/3. Exact arithmetic verifies D²=2I-D+J, U²=3I+W and UW=2U and the three even/three odd Legendre Gram eigensectors. Direct independent kernel arithmetic checks each sector for all degrees 0–61, giving the stated exact ranks and no further zeros through 61. The classical Bernstein Legendre bound and rigorous rational coefficient bounds give strict diagonal dominance for every degree at least 62, proving all-degree recovery. Pseudoinverse interpolation and minimal-norm assertions follow from Hilbert-space reproducing-kernel linear algebra. Verification code is embedded and executable; no finite experiment substitutes for the infinite analytic step.

value.rationale: The ten axes of a regular dodecahedron are an invariant natural finite sampling orbit. Individual-degree harmonic data exhibit rank reversal from degree four (9) to five (6), first full recovery at six, exceptional rank-nine degrees eight and fourteen, and permanent recovery only from degree fifteen. The all-degree exact sector spectrum gives explicit feasibility and minimum-norm interpolation and includes a rigorous uniform tail theorem, not an arbitrary one-off table or textbook corollary.
